deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivations, formulas or computations. It is a clean copy, apparently in an editor's or copyist's hand, with later pencil annotations. It assembles several of Riemann's natural-philosophy fragments ('Blatt 7', 'Blatt 8', the closing part of the causality fragment). Nothing on it can be restated as a derivation. Its content, in order:

(a) Conclusion of the argument begun on p. 9. Observed change is continuous: no jump is perceived, and continuity is preferred over many tiny jumps. By the already-confirmed concept of things existing for themselves (für sich bestehende Dinge), one infers that a thing would stay what it is if nothing else were added. This is the source of the drive to seek a cause for every change. So the concepts of continuous change and of causality arise together, as a minimal revision of the concept of self-subsistent things.

(b) Pencil editorial note: perhaps attach here pp. 1–3, 'Lebenslauf' (Blatt 2). Also '(bis hierher 1.)' and, opposite the list of works, 'Wohl wegzulassen?' ('probably omit?').

(c) Bracketed summary. The task of explaining nature is to recognise the connection of things from the connection of appearances. This presupposes the contrast between appearances and things, and the formation of the concept of self-subsistent things.

(d) Blatt 7: Riemann's self-description of his current work, a well-known passage connected with his Habilitation/application of c. 1853–54.
  1. Introducing the imaginary into the theory of other transcendental functions, as already done for algebraic, exponential/circular, elliptic and Abelian functions. The 'necessary general preliminaries' are said to be in his Inaugural Dissertation, Art. 20.
  2. New methods for integrating partial differential equations, already applied to physical problems, especially in electricity.
  3. His main work: a new conception of the known laws of nature, expressed through other basic concepts. This would allow use of the experimental data on the interaction between heat, (light, magnetism, electricity …); the sentence breaks off.

(e) Blatt 8: references to Leibniz's letters to Des Bosses S.J. (p. 294, Hannover 15 Feb 1712; p. 320, 29 May 1716, with the postscript apologising for his very disturbed handwriting). A pencil margin note reads 'Leibnitz'.

(f) Remarks on 'hypothesis': the word now means something somewhat different than for Newton. Today one calls a hypothesis everything added in thought to the appearances. This leads into Newton's 'hypotheses non fingo' on p. 11.
errors: No mathematical steps, so no mathematical errors. Item 3 of the work list breaks off mid-sentence ('zwischen Wärme'); this is an incomplete fragment, not an error.

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely philosophical and biographical material. It is already known and published: the work list is quoted in Dedekind's biography, and the causality and hypothesis fragments appear in the Werke's philosophical fragments. There is no mathematics on the page.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially accurate. The pencil note reads 'S. 1 – 3: Lebenslauf (Blatt 2)'; 'Lebenslauf' is underlined, and the '[?]' can probably be dropped.
'Wohl wegzulassen?' is a pencil margin note placed opposite the list of works (items 1–3), not part of the main text.
'Leibnitz' and '(3)' are faint pencil margin annotations beside Blatt 8, not part of the text.
